verdict.rationale: Viam's own logic modules are documented for exactly this purpose: running continuous processes, scheduling actions, and reacting to sensor data with alerts or actuator commands on the machine without a person involved. They can be written in the browser as inline modules, with Viam managing builds and deployment. Machines also pull trained models automatically, and data sync handles outages on its own. Missing for 10: detailed documentation of the scheduling and background-execution mechanism, any no-code automation builder (automations need module code), and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can set up automations that run autonomously in the background

citations.quote: Use a logic module when you need your machine to: React to sensor data... Coordinate multiple components... Run continuous processes... Schedule actions
React to sensor data: trigger an alert or an actuator when a reading crosses a threshold.
A temperature sensor crosses a threshold, and a notification fires.
Inline modules let you write code directly in the Viam app's browser-based editor. Viam manages source code, builds, versioning, and deployment.
Machines pull them automatically and run inference locally.
